```{r}
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
```

# Data Sets
```{r}

# 1. Course Data
course_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wkessler-oss/PGA-Tour-ML-Analysis/main/Course%20Data.csv"
course_data <- read_csv(course_url)

# 2. Player Data
master_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wkessler-oss/PGA-Tour-ML-Analysis/main/PGA_2025_Master.csv"
pga_master <- read_csv(master_url)

pga_master <- pga_master %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean to_par
    to_par = case_when(
      to_par == "E" ~ "0",
      TRUE ~ to_par
    ),
    to_par = as.numeric(to_par),
    
    # Convert all round scores and total to numeric
    r1    = as.numeric(r1),
    r2    = as.numeric(r2),
    r3    = as.numeric(r3),
    r4    = as.numeric(r4),
    total = as.numeric(total)
  )

# Make sure it came in correctly
head(course_data)
head(pga_master)
```

## Data Set Descriptions

### Player Data

The dataset comes from official PGA Tour performace tacking sustems, which come from ShotLink. This is a swing data collection from high speed cameras, and other ,easurements on every hole. This Data is from the 2024-2025 PGA tour season, and includes Driving Distance, Green in Regulation, Strokes gained, and results. 

### Assumptions

We assume that the season averages of a players swing will be consistent week to week, not intaking the varience within it
This can be a risk becuase they could be injured or just fatigued from the season. Meaning that our dataset would not accuretly predict the cut.

Another assumption is that the players metrics are inherit to the player, and not to the course.
This is a risk becasue ofgten time players will be more comfortable on a course if they have played it more, or they will play more aggressive if they know the course.

### Course Data

The course data is from a PGA tour website, which analyses the courses architecture. It includes yardages, par, grass types, and other things like distance and hazards. 

### Assumptions
We assume that the courses do not chainge, such as the tee boxes do not move, and they do not change any hazards or conditions. 
This assumption is risky because conditions on tournament days can be super variable. THings such as wind and humidity can affect the way a ball flies immensely.

Another assuumption is that course paramteters affect all players the same
This is a risk because condition changes on a course may affect short vs long hitters very differently.

## Looking For Outliers
```{r}
pga_master %>%
  select(r1, r2, r3, r4, total, to_par, sg_total, sg_ott, sg_app, sg_arg, sg_putt, sg_rounds) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "Individual Variable Distributions (Histograms)",
    subtitle = "Examine distribution shape, center, and tail extremes",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```
### There does not seem to be many outliers. The difference in rounds and total line up becasuse the total will be less if there is less rounds.



# Plotting
```{r}
ggplot(data = pga_master, aes(x = sg_ott, y = sg_app)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Strokes Gained: Off-the-Tee vs. Approach",
    x = "Strokes Gained: Off-the-Tee (Driving)",
    y = "Strokes Gained: Approach (Iron Play)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
pga_master %>%
  inner_join(course_data, by = c("course_name" = "course")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = adj_driving_distance, y = sg_ott)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Course Adjusted Driving Distance vs. Player SG: Off-the-Tee",
    x = "Course Adjusted Driving Distance (Yards)",
    y = "Strokes Gained: Off-the-Tee (Driving Performance)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```
```{r}
pga_master %>%
  inner_join(course_data, by = c("course_name" = "course")) %>%
  group_by(player) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_course_dist = mean(adj_driving_distance, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_sg_ott      = mean(sg_ott, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_sg_total    = mean(sg_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    events          = n(),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(events >= 5) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = avg_course_dist, y = avg_sg_ott)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_point(aes(color = avg_sg_total, size = events), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Avg SG: Total") +
  labs(
    title = "Player Driving Performance vs. Course Driving Distance",
    subtitle = "Min. 5 events played in 2025 season",
    x = "Average Course Driving Distance (Yards)",
    y = "Average Strokes Gained: Off-the-Tee",
    size = "Events Played"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```
```{r}

pga_master %>%
  inner_join(course_data, by = c("course_name" = "course")) %>%
  group_by(player) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_course_dist = mean(adj_driving_distance, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_sg_ott      = mean(sg_ott, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_to_par      = mean(to_par, na.rm = TRUE),
    events          = n(),
    .groups         = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(events >= 5) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = avg_course_dist, y = avg_to_par)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = avg_sg_ott, size = events), alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = player), max.overlaps = 12, size = 3) +
  scale_y_reverse() + # Reverse axis: lower score to par is better
  scale_color_gradient(low = "orange", high = "darkgreen", name = "Avg SG: OTT") +
  labs(
    title = "Player Scoring to Par vs. Course Driving Distance",
    subtitle = "Lower score to par is better (y-axis inverted)",
    x = "Average Course Driving Distance (Yards)",
    y = "Average Score to Par"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```
